parole.significato: abbot (the superior or head of an abbey or monastery)
parole.testo: A loanword of debated origin: # Borrowed from Serbo-Croatian or Slovene opat (“abbot”). # Borrowed from Old High German abbat (“abbot”), from Latin abbas (“father”), from Ancient Greek ἀββᾶς (abbâs) In both cases, ultimately from Aramaic אבא (’abbā, “father”).
Borrowed from Serbo-Croatian kup and Slovene kup. First attested in 1713.
From Serbo-Croatian pakao or Slovene pekel. From Proto-Slavic *pьkъlъ.

parole.significato: broom (any plant of the genus Genista)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Serbo-Croatian rakitje or Slovene rakitje. First attested in 1181.

parole.significato: to knock up (to put together hastily or without effective equipment)
parole.testo: From Serbo-Croatian tȁk/та̏к (“shoe heel”) or Slovene, itself from Italian tacco + -ol (“verb-forming suffix”).
Borrowed Serbo-Croatian or Slovene, compare Serbo-Croatian žížak, dialectal žižek, Slovene žižek (“weevil”).

parole.significato: flag, standard, banner, ensign (piece of cloth, often decorated with an emblem, used as a visual signal or symbol)
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Serbo-Croatian zastava or Slovene zastava. For the sound change /st/ > /sl/, compare poroszló and boroszlán. Compare Slovak zástava. First attested in 1086.
